A canonical artifact manifest defines the exact bounded artifact-ref roster and derives one 64-hex digest with deterministic ordering/encoding; the record is cross-bound to projectId, attemptRef, input/result manifest identities and resultTreeSha256 so receipt or worktree digests cannot be substituted.

The real Foundation result/evidence production path writes the artifact manifest before the receipt/release consumer can observe it, and a strict project+attempt reader revalidates canonical bytes, digest, cardinality, bindings and a stable horizon. Caller input may name artifacts but cannot supply the authoritative digest or truth.

Absent, stale, foreign, ambiguous, malformed, corrupt, reordered, duplicate or moved-horizon manifests refuse with exact wrapper and source code/layer and no event movement; byte-identical replay is idempotent and conflicting bytes are fenced.

Exact code/layer, TDD, <=250-line target per focused production source, explicit-path commits, preserve foreign work.

implementationPlan.description:
THE ARTIFACT MANIFEST CONTRACT - new module apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-artifact-manifest.ts plus its one-line .js bridge (every production sibling in this directory has one; a missing bridge is invisible to both tsc and vitest). It defines the bounded roster, derives ONE 64-hex canonical digest with deterministic ordering and encoding, and owns its own closed code list and layer.

CONDITION 1 OF THE RULING LIVES HERE, AND ITS HARD PART IS CHOOSING THE DENOMINATOR. The sealed empty must be provably distinguishable from never-enumerated. THE OBVIOUS DENOMINATOR IS A TRAP: a count taken from the capture's enumerated surfaces - result-tree entries or authored paths - can legitimately be ZERO for an attempt that changed nothing, so a zero denominator would mean BOTH observed-nothing and never-ran, and condition 1 collapses back into the defect it exists to prevent. Pick a denominator that cannot read zero when the scan ran.

WHAT TO USE INSTEAD, both parts required: (a) the BINDING - the sealed body carries the capture's own resultManifest sha256, which exists if and only if the capture answered and buildResultManifest succeeded (foundation-attempt-store.ts:222-228); a roster nobody enumerated has no such value to bind to. (b) the OBSERVATION - an explicit artifactRefCount, 0 here, stated rather than inferred from an array's length at read time. The binding proves enumeration happened; the count states what it saw. Cross-bind projectId, attemptRef and the input-manifest identity per DoD 1.

RAIL 1 IS ABSOLUTE: this digest seals the ARTIFACT ROSTER only. Never derive it from, alias it to, or fall back on receiptSha256, resultTreeSha256, inputDigest or worktreeDigest. The result-manifest digest already covers declaredArtifactRefs in its own preimage (workspace-manifest.ts:230-237) - that is a DIFFERENT fact and reusing it is the substitution DoD 4 mutation-drills.

Do not edit anything under packages/runner. The foundation-workspace-capture.ts:217-220 pin is the invariant this row preserves, and it lives in another package.
implementationPlan.note:
THE ARTIFACT MANIFEST CONTRACT — new `apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-artifact-manifest.ts`, **229 lines** (250 target), plus its one-line LF `.js` bridge `export * from "./foundation-artifact-manifest.ts";` (verified LF, not CRLF, by `od -c`: the file ends `" ; \n`). Layer `DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ARTIFACT` is module-private with only the TYPE exported, matching `release-handoff-binding.ts` — a runtime column-zero `*_LAYER` export is a declared boundary the security roster then polices.

`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` EXIT 0 with the `$ tsc --project tsconfig.json` echo.

**THE DENOMINATOR I CHOSE, AND WHY IT CANNOT READ ZERO WHEN THE SCAN RAN** (condition 1 of the ruling; this is the answer QA said they will verify). Two parts, both required, exactly as the step prescribes:
- **BINDING** — `resultManifestSha256`, validated as 64-hex before anything is derived. It exists if and only if the capture answered AND `buildResultManifest` succeeded (`foundation-attempt-store.ts:222-228`). A roster nobody enumerated has no such value to bind to, so the seal refuses `FOUNDATION_ARTIFACT_BINDING_INCOMPLETE` rather than emitting a bare `[]`.
- **OBSERVATION** — `artifactRefCount` is a STATED field on the durable body, not `artifactRefs.length` recomputed at read time. A count that is only ever recomputed from the array cannot testify that the scan ran.

I explicitly did NOT use an enumerated result-tree or authored-path count: those are legitimately zero for an attempt that changed nothing, so zero would mean both "observed nothing" and "never ran" and condition 1 would collapse into the defect it exists to prevent.

**RAIL 1, AND ONE MEASUREMENT THAT MAKES THE TRAP SHARPER THAN THE PLAN STATED.** The digest preimage is `{artifactRefCount, artifactRefs, manifestVersion}` — the ROSTER ONLY. The cross-bindings (`projectId`, `attemptRef`, `inputManifestSha256`, `resultManifestSha256`) ride BESIDE the digest on the record, not inside the preimage; folding them in would make it a compound identity that changes when nothing about the artifacts did, and the reader is the right place to refuse a foreign binding. New measurement worth recording: `packages/runner/src/evidence/evidence-receipt.ts:202` and `:217` set `resultTreeSha256: input.resultManifest.sha256` — **so `resultManifestSha256` and `resultTreeSha256` are the SAME VALUE on this lane.** That means drill 3's substitution (return `resultManifest.sha256` as the artifact digest) is literally returning `resultTreeSha256`, which rail 1 names by name. The substitution is more tempting than it looks and arm E is what makes the rule a test.

**A DESIGN DECISION THAT DIVERGES FROM A NARROW READING OF THE PLAN, stated so QA can reject it now rather than at the end.** The plan's step 3 says the Foundation-lane nonempty fence goes in the ledger, and I have kept **no lane policy in this module** — `sealFoundationArtifactManifest` is total over any bounded, well-formed roster. The reason is not convenience: if the fence lived here, `canonicalArtifactRoster`'s ORDERING would be unreachable code (no nonempty roster could ever reach the sort), and drill 4 (order-dependent hashing) could only red a test of dead code. With the fence one layer up, ordering stability is testable against a real nonempty roster through a production surface. Condition 2 is enforced in step 3 as the ruling requires; it is not weakened, it is placed where it does not blind a drill.

WHAT THE MODULE REFUSES, each with its own stable code under `DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ARTIFACT`:
- `FOUNDATION_ARTIFACT_BINDING_INCOMPLETE` — absent/short `attemptRef` or `projectId`, or a non-hex64 `resultManifestSha256`/`inputManifestSha256`. This is the not-enumerated arm at the contract layer.
- `FOUNDATION_ARTIFACT_ROSTER_MALFORMED` — not an array; a ref that is not EXACTLY `{byteLength, sha256}` (exact keys, not a subset — an extra member would ride into the preimage unvalidated and change the digest); a non-hex64 sha256; a negative or non-safe-integer byteLength; **or a DUPLICATE ref**.
- `FOUNDATION_ARTIFACT_ROSTER_OVERSIZE` — more than `MAX_FOUNDATION_ARTIFACT_REFS` (512), so the preimage cannot be made unbounded.
- `FOUNDATION_ARTIFACT_MANIFEST_UNSEALABLE` — the canonical encoder refused.

**DUPLICATES REFUSE RATHER THAN DEDUPE**, deliberately: two identical refs in one roster is a caller that lost count, and silently collapsing them would seal a cardinality nobody declared — the same class of manufactured fact as the bare `[]`.

Nothing under `packages/runner` was touched; the `foundation-workspace-capture.ts:217-220` pin is untouched and is the invariant this row preserves.

implementationPlan.description:
THE DURABLE LEDGER - new module apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-artifact-ledger.ts plus its .js bridge: one append-only write on its own derived aggregate, and one strict project+attempt reader.

COPY THE SHAPE ALREADY PROVEN ON THIS LANE - apps/daemon/src/work/release-handoff-binding.ts is the model and is worth reading before writing a line. Take from it: an aggregate id derived per attempt and NOT content-addressed (so a re-seal appends rather than colliding); commitExpectedVersionDecision at the measured head; replay-idempotence on IDENTICAL bytes with a real conflict on differing bytes rather than a second truth; and a reader that re-decodes AND re-encodes and BYTE-COMPARES against the stored payload, because two objects can be deep-equal while their canonical bytes differ.

THE READER (DoD 2 and 3) refuses ABSENT, foreign-project, ambiguous, malformed, drifted, reordered, duplicate and moved-horizon rows, each with a stable code, and carries any upstream code and layer UNRESTAMPED. ABSENT is the NOT-ENUMERATED arm of condition 1 and needs its own code distinct from every other refusal - that specific code and layer is what QA said they will verify, so it must be assertable and must never be reachable from an observed-empty seal.

THE FOUNDATION-LANE NEGATIVE CONTROL (condition 2) IS ENFORCED HERE, and its placement is the whole point. The seal REFUSES a nonempty roster on this lane with its own stable code. Put the fence in the daemon, NOT in packages/runner and NOT in the shared sealer: workspace-manifest.ts:214 canonicalArtifactRefs legitimately accepts nonempty refs from OTHER producers, so a fence there would break them, and the runner's pin is the invariant being preserved rather than a place to add code. This is defence in depth for a rationale that currently lives one package away - and note the direction, because it decides whether QA passes this row: the change makes the Foundation lane REFUSE caller-handed refs, never willing to seal them.

**CONDITION 2 OF THE RULING IS ENFORCED HERE, AND IT RUNS FIRST.** `sealFoundationArtifactRoster` refuses `FOUNDATION_ARTIFACT_LEDGER_ROSTER_UNAUTHORIZED` on a nonempty offered roster **before the manifest is derived at all** — a caller-handed roster never reaches a digest. The direction is the one the ruling demands: this lane REFUSES caller-supplied refs; it is never willing to seal them. Placement is per the plan — not in `packages/runner` (the `foundation-workspace-capture.ts:217-220` pin is the invariant being preserved and I touched nothing there), and not in the shared sealer (`workspace-manifest.ts:214` legitimately accepts nonempty refs from OTHER producers, so a fence there would break them).

**CONDITION 1's ASYMMETRY, stated as the property the arms will test:** an observed-empty seal WRITES A ROW, so the reader finds one and can never answer ABSENT. `FOUNDATION_ARTIFACT_LEDGER_ABSENT` is therefore reachable only when nothing was ever enumerated, and it is a distinct code from every other refusal here. That is what makes "sealed zero" and "nobody looked" different durable outcomes rather than two readings of one `[]`.

READER REFUSALS, each its own stable code under `DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ARTIFACT_LEDGER`: `ABSENT` (not-enumerated), `AMBIGUOUS` (duplicate aggregate sequence), `PROJECT_MISMATCH`, `ATTEMPT_MISMATCH` (via `readFoundationArtifactForAttempt` — a manifest sealed under X is not evidence about Y even inside the right project), `DRIFT` (decode/re-encode/byte-compare failed, or the body's key set is not exactly the eight), `HORIZON_MOVED`, `CONFLICT`, `UNREADABLE`. The manifest layer's codes travel out **UNRESTAMPED** with `sealed.layer`, because a binding this daemon could not assemble and a roster the caller malformed demand opposite repairs.

**TWO GUARDS I ADDED BEYOND THE STEP TEXT, both because the step's own reasoning implies them:**
1. **The stated count is re-checked against the roster it describes** (`count !== refs.length` → `DRIFT`). `artifactRefCount` is the observation half of condition 1's denominator; a row whose declared cardinality disagrees with its own refs is not evidence, and without this check the "stated, not recomputed" design would let a drifted row assert a scan that never matched.
2. **The horizon check is AGGREGATE-SCOPED**, re-reading the same aggregate after the decode and refusing `HORIZON_MOVED` if the row count changed. A GLOBAL horizon check moves on any unrelated write and would refuse nearly every read on a busy daemon — this one moves only if THIS roster moved.

**ONE CORRECTION AGAINST THE MODEL, worth recording because copying it blindly would not have compiled.** `release-handoff-binding.ts` takes its durable instant from `newest.occurredAt` — but that is a JOURNAL ENTRY, not a `StoredEvent`. `StoredEvent` (`store-contracts.ts:175-195`) has **no `occurredAt`**; the store's own stamp is `committedAt`. First typecheck caught it as `TS2339: Property 'occurredAt' does not exist on type 'StoredEvent'`. `committedAt` on an already-existing row is equally a durable instant and equally reproducible on re-derivation, so the no-clock-read discipline holds — but the two types are not interchangeable and the model's field name does not transfer.

**THE ORDERING, which is the requirement and not an implementation detail.** In `recordProvenFoundationAttempt` the seal sits between `buildResultManifest` and `settleFoundationAttempt`:
```
if (!built.ok) return advisory(built.code, RUNNER_WORKSPACE_LAYER);
const sealed = sealFoundationArtifactRoster(store, {...});   <- AFTER the manifest, so
if (!sealed.ok) return advisory(sealed.code, sealed.layer);     its sha256 is available
return settleFoundationAttempt(..., truthClass: "PROVEN", null);  <- BEFORE the settle
```

A seal landing after the settle is observable-too-late by definition; the consumer must not be able to see a PROVEN attempt whose `artifactDigest` has no producer.

Silently settling PROVEN without the seal is precisely the gap this row was filed to close, so the refusal arm is load-bearing rather than defensive.

implementationPlan.description:
THE SUITE (DoD 4 as amended) - apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-artifact-ledger.test.ts, file-backed SqliteEventStore, traversing the REAL production writer. The nonempty-roster control is amended OUT by the ruling; these arms replace it.

A. AUTHORIZED-EMPTY, SEALED. Drive a real proven capture through recordProvenFoundationAttempt and assert the durable artifact manifest exists with a 64-hex digest, artifactRefCount 0, and the binding to the capture's own resultManifest sha256. Assert raw event counts read OUT OF THE STORE, not from the return value.

B. CONDITION 1, BOTH SIDES, WHICH IS THE ARM QA SAID THEY WILL ACTUALLY VERIFY. Observed-empty (A) and NOT-ENUMERATED must produce DIFFERENT durable outcomes. Reach not-enumerated honestly - an attempt whose capture never answered, which foundation-attempt-store.ts:215-217 already refuses as FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_CAPTURE_UNKNOWN - and assert the reader answers its ABSENT code at its own layer with ZERO artifact rows written. Assert the specific code and the layer, per epic rail 6, never merely that it refused.

C. CONDITION 2, THE NEGATIVE CONTROL. A nonempty roster offered on the Foundation lane is REFUSED with the exact code and layer, and no row is written.
